definitions.meaning: Ireland, where the Scottas lived before migrating to the country now called Scotland

quotations.old_english: Án diácon wearð forþféred on Sceot-lande (cf. an Scotta eálonde, 215, 21), and ðæs diácones nama wæs Njál háten
Hér fór Æþelstán cyning on Scotland (tó Scotlande in Scotiam, MS. F.)
Hé (Cnut) fór tó Scotlande, and Scotta cyng him tó beáh, Mælcolm
Hé (Fursetis) férde geond eal Ýrrland and Scotland

source_text: Scot-land, es; n. I. Ireland, where the Scottas lived before migrating to the country now called Scotland:--On westende (of Europe) is Scotland, Ors. 1, 1; Swt. 8, 27. Án diácon wearð forþféred on Sceot&dash-uncertain;lande (cf. an Scotta eálonde, 215, 21), and ðæs diácones nama wæs Njál háten, Wulfst. 205, 16. Hí cómon on Scotland (Hiberniam) upp, Bd. l, l; S. 474, 10. II. Scotland:--Hér fór Æþelstán cyning on Scotland (tó Scotlande in Scotiam, MS. F.), Chr. 934; Erl. 111, 9. Hé (Cnut) fór tó Scotlande, and Scotta cyng him tó beáh, Mælcolm, 1031; Erl. 163, 20. Hé (Fursetis) férde geond eal Ýrrland and Scotland, Homl. Th. ii. 346, 29. v. Scottas
